words.textHint: You lie down on it at night and sleep under the covers.
The soft squishy thing you rest your head on when you sleep.
The big soft cover you snuggle under to stay warm in bed.
A long soft seat where the whole family can sit together.
A seat with four legs and a back that one person sits on.
A flat top with legs where you eat dinner or do homework.
You click it on to light up a room at night, and it often sits on a little table.
You open it to walk into a room and close it behind you.
The glass part of the wall you look through to see outside.
It has hands or numbers that tell you what time it is.
A small metal thing you turn to unlock the front door.
You drink milk, water, or juice out of it.
You use it to scoop up soup and cereal.
It has pointy tips for picking up food to eat.
The flat round dish you put your dinner on.
A round deep dish you eat cereal or soup from.
You use it to cut your food into little pieces.
The slippery bubbly bar you scrub with to get clean.
A big soft cloth you use to dry off after a bath.
The little brush with a handle you use to clean your teeth.
The minty goo you squeeze onto your brush to clean your teeth.
You fill it with warm water and sit in it to get clean.
The seat in the bathroom that you flush after using it.
The bowl with a faucet where you wash your hands and the dishes.
The shiny glass you look into to see your own face.
A flat tool with skinny teeth for making your hair neat.
You sweep the dusty floor with it.
A round container with a handle for carrying water or sand.
You throw garbage and old wrappers into it.
You hold it to your ear to talk to someone far away.
The big screen in the living room where you watch cartoons.
A machine with a keyboard and a screen you use for games and homework.
You point it at people and click to take a picture.
The big cold box in the kitchen that keeps your food fresh.
A hot box in the kitchen where you bake cookies and pizza.
It spins around fast to blow cool air on you on a hot day.
A wax stick with a little flame that you blow out on your birthday cake.
Steps you climb to go up or down inside a house.
The very top part of a house that keeps the rain out.
The flat sides of a room where you hang pictures.
The flat part of a room that you walk on.
The room in the house where meals are cooked.
The room with the toilet, the sink, and the tub.
The room where you sleep at night.
A place outside the house where flowers and vegetables grow.
You hold it over your head so the rain does not get you wet.
The bag you carry on your back with your school books inside.
You wear them on your nose to help you see better.
You wear it on top of your head.
A soft head cover with a curvy part in front to block the sun.
You wear it on the top half of your body, with your arms through the sleeves.
You put one leg in each side and pull them up.
A one-piece outfit that kids often twirl around in.
A piece of clothing that hangs from your waist, like the bottom part of a dress.
The soft thing you put on your foot before your shoe goes on.
You wear it on your foot when you walk outside.
Tall shoes you wear to stomp in puddles or snow.
A big warm layer you put on over everything when it is freezing outside.
A short coat you zip up when the wind gets chilly.
A long soft thing you wrap around your neck in winter.
You wear them on your hands, and each finger gets its own spot.
Warm hand covers where only your thumb gets its own spot.
The comfy clothes you change into before bed.
A warm knitted top you pull over your head in winter.
The little round thing you push through a hole to close your shirt.
You pull it up and down to open and close your jacket.
The little pouch on your pants where you keep small things.
You wear it around your waist to hold your pants up.
A small circle of metal you wear on your finger.
You wear it on your wrist so you can tell the time.
The round top part of your body where your brain lives.
The part at the end of your arm with five fingers.
The part at the bottom of your leg that you stand on.
The long part of your body you use to walk, run, and kick.
The long part between your shoulder and your hand that swings when you walk.
The two things on the sides of your head that you listen with.
The part in the middle of your face that you smell with.
You blink them, and you use them to see everything.
The part of your face you use to eat and talk.
The wiggly pink thing inside your mouth that tastes food.
One of the hard white things in your mouth that chew your food.
One of the five long parts on your hand that you point with.
One of the five little wiggly parts at the end of your foot.
The bendy middle part of your leg.
The part of your body that connects your head to your shoulders.
It grows on top of your head, and you brush it every morning.
The part of your body where your arm connects, and where a backpack strap rests.
The soft front part of your body that growls when you are hungry.
The pointy bendy part in the middle of your arm.
The short thick finger you point up when something is great.
The soft round part of your face that grandmas love to pinch.
The very bottom point of your face, under your mouth.
A tall cabinet with doors where you hang your shirts and coats.
A piece of bedroom furniture with drawers where you keep folded clothes.
A tall piece of furniture with flat boards for lining up all your books.
Two sleeping spots stacked on top of each other, with a ladder to reach the top.
A seat with curved bottoms that tips gently back and forth.
A small seat with legs but no back, often found at a kitchen counter.
A tiny rocking bed made for a baby.
The big soft bouncy part of a bed that you actually lie on.
A soft squishy pad that makes a chair or couch comfy to sit on.
The cloth hanging over a window that you pull closed to block the light.
The soft fuzzy covering on a floor that feels nice on bare feet.
The rough little rug by the front door where you wipe your shoes.
Visitors push this button outside your house to make a ding-dong sound.
The box outside your house where letters and packages are delivered.
The tall pipe on a roof where smoke comes out, and where Santa is said to climb down.
A special spot in the wall where a cozy fire burns to warm the room.
The room at the very top of a house, under the roof, where old boxes are stored.
The room underneath a house, down the stairs below the first floor.
The room with a big rolling door where the family car is parked.
A small space behind a door where you hang clothes and hide toys.
The long skinny walking space that connects the rooms of a house.
The covered area at the front of a house where you might sit outside.
The flat part of a room above your head that you see when you lie on the floor.
You turn its handle and water comes pouring out into the sink.
The hole at the bottom of the tub or sink where the water swirls away.
You stand under it while warm water rains down on you to get clean.
The special soap you rub into your hair to make it clean and bubbly.
The thin string you slide between your teeth to clean out stuck food.
The sticky strip you put over a cut or scrape to protect it.
The soft thin paper you grab from a box to blow your nose.
The small snipping tool used to trim your fingernails when they get long.
A machine that blows hot air to dry your wet hair fast.
The big pile of dirty clothes waiting to be washed.
The machine that spins your dirty clothes around in soapy water.
A loud machine you push around that sucks up dirt from the floor.
The machine in the kitchen that washes all the dirty plates for you.
The kitchen box that beeps and heats up your food in just a minute.
You drop bread in it, and it pops up warm and crunchy.
A loud spinning machine that turns fruit and ice into a smoothie.
A pot with a spout that heats water and sometimes whistles when it is ready.
The flat pan with a long handle used to cook eggs and pancakes.
You tie it over your clothes so they stay clean while you cook.
The thick padded glove you wear so hot pans do not burn your hand.
The square of paper or cloth you use to wipe your mouth at dinner.
Two thin sticks some people use to pick up their food.
The little box on the wall you set to make the house warmer or cooler.
You press its buttons from the couch to change the channel on the TV.
A little tube you click on to shine a beam of light in the dark.
The small power stick you put inside toys and remotes to make them work.
You flip it on the wall to turn the lights on and off.
It rings loudly in the morning to wake you up for school.
You wear them over your ears to listen to music that only you can hear.
The heavy tool you swing to pound nails into wood.
The tool you twist to tighten the little metal spirals that hold things together.
You climb its steps to reach high places, like painting a wall or getting on the roof.
A tool with two blades that open and close to cut paper.
A bendy strip with numbers that pulls out to check how long something is.
The sturdy box where hammers, wrenches, and nails are kept.
The long bendy tube in the yard that sprays water on the plants.
A tool with long teeth you drag across the yard to gather fallen leaves.
You push it into the dirt to dig a hole.
The little strip of hair above each of your eyes.
The tiny hairs on the edge of your eyelids that flutter when you blink.
The bendy joint that connects your foot to your leg.
The bendy joint between your hand and your arm, where a watch goes.
The flat part of your face above your eyebrows and below your hair.
The round back part of your foot.
All the bones inside your body put together.
The strong stretchy parts inside your arms and legs that help you move and lift.
The part inside your chest that thumps and pumps blood around your body.
The two parts inside your chest that fill with air when you breathe in.
The part inside your head that does all your thinking.
The part inside your belly where your food goes after you swallow it.
The long line of bones that runs down the middle of your back.
The hard flat part on the tip of each finger that keeps growing.
The big slow mouth-opening thing you do when you are sleepy.
The big ah-choo that bursts out of your nose.
The funny little jumping sound your body makes over and over that you cannot stop.
